QF.id: Taxation of Debt and Equity Products_C1_5

question.text: Scenario: Anita Desai, aged 45, is a resident Indian in the 30% tax bracket (old regime). During FY 2025-26, she has the following investment transactions: 1. Equity Mutual Fund A: Purchased 5,000 units at Rs. 120 per unit on 15-Mar-2024. Sold all units at Rs. 155 per unit on 20-Jan-2026. STT paid on sale. 2. Equity Mutual Fund B: Purchased 3,000 units at Rs. 200 per unit on 10-Aug-2025. Sold all units at Rs. 185 per unit on 25-Feb-2026. STT paid on sale. 3. Debt Mutual Fund C (invested 90% in debt securities): Purchased 10,000 units at Rs. 50 per unit on 05-May-2024. Sold all units at Rs. 54 per unit on 15-Nov-2025. This fund was purchased after 1-Apr-2023. 4. Bank Fixed Deposit: Rs. 15,00,000 at 7.5% p.a. for 1 year, matured on 30-Sep-2025. TDS deducted at 10%. 5. Dividend received from Equity MF A during holding period: Rs. 25,000 (TDS of 10% deducted as dividend exceeded Rs. 5,000). 6. Arbitrage Fund D (an equity-oriented mutual fund that holds at least 65% of net assets in domestic equity and equity-related instruments, qualifying as equity-oriented under the Income-tax Act): Purchased 8,000 units at Rs. 15 per unit on 01-Feb-2025. Sold all units at Rs. 16.50 per unit on 10-Mar-2026. STT paid on sale. Anita's total salary income (after standard deduction) is Rs. 22,00,000. She has no other income or deductions. Question 5 of 5: What is the net taxable LTCG under section 112A after aggregating all eligible gains and losses, and what is the final tax on this amount?

answer.text: Net taxable LTCG under s.112A = Rs. 17,000 after set-off and exemption; tax at 12.5% = Rs. 2,125
Net taxable LTCG under s.112A = Rs. 50,000 after exemption on MF A alone; tax at 12.5% = Rs. 6,250
Net taxable LTCG under s.112A = Rs. 62,000 after exemption; tax at 12.5% = Rs. 7,750
Net taxable LTCG under s.112A = Rs. 1,42,000 (no exemption available as total gains exceed Rs. 1.25 lakh); tax at 12.5% = Rs. 17,750

explanation.text: The Logic: Step-by-step computation of net LTCG under section 112A: Step 1 - Identify all section 112A gains and losses: (a) Equity MF A: LTCG (held >12 months, STT paid) = (Rs. 155 - Rs. 120) x 5,000 = Rs. 1,75,000 (b) Arbitrage Fund D: Stem confirms it is an equity-oriented MF (>=65% domestic equity), STT paid. Held from 01-Feb-2025 to 10-Mar-2026 = approximately 13 months (>12 months) = LTCG. Gain = (Rs. 16.50 - Rs. 15) x 8,000 = Rs. 12,000 (c) Total gross LTCG under 112A = Rs. 1,75,000 + Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 1,87,000 Step 2 - Set-off of short-term capital loss: Equity MF B resulted in STCL of Rs. 45,000 (under s.111A). STCL can be set off against LTCG. After set-off: Rs. 1,87,000 - Rs. 45,000 = Rs. 1,42,000. Step 3 - Apply Rs. 1,25,000 exemption under s.112A: Taxable LTCG = Rs. 1,42,000 - Rs. 1,25,000 = Rs. 17,000. Step 4 - Compute tax: Tax = 12.5% x Rs. 17,000 = Rs. 2,125 (plus applicable cess). The Trap: Option B ignores the Arbitrage Fund D gain and the set-off of MF B loss. Option C miscalculates the set-off. Option D wrongly states the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption is unavailable when total gains exceed Rs. 1.25 lakh - the exemption always applies to the first Rs. 1.25 lakh of LTCG under 112A; only the excess is taxed. The audit flagged the original item because Arbitrage Fund D's equity-oriented status was not stated; the s.112A aggregation only works if that fund meets the 65% domestic equity test. Note: The original stem said only "Arbitrage Fund D" with STT paid, without confirming equity-oriented MF status (which under the Income-tax Act requires at least 65% of net assets in domestic equity). The stem has been tightened to expressly state that Arbitrage Fund D meets the 65% domestic equity test and qualifies as equity-oriented, which makes the s.112A aggregation and the Rs. 17,000 / Rs. 2,125 figures uniquely correct (NISM Series X-B pp.240, 243-245, 162-163).
